+package io.netty.handler.codec.http2;
+
+/**
+ * HTTP/2 Push Promise Read Frame
+ */
+public interface Http2PushPromiseRead extends Http2StreamFrame {
+
+    /**
+     * Promised Stream-ID sent in Push Promise
+     */
+    int promisedStreamId();
+
+    /**
+     * {@link Http2Headers} sent in Push Promise
+     */
+    Http2Headers http2Headers();
+
+    /**
+     * Frame padding to use. Will be non-negative and less than 256.
+     */
+    int padding();
+}

timeline.body:
Motivation:
Right now, we don't have to handle Push Promise Read in `Http2FrameCodec`. Push Promise is one of the key features of HTTP/2 and we should support it in our `Http2FrameCodec`.

Modification:
Added `Http2PushPromiseFrame` and `Http2PushPromiseFrame` to handle Push Promise and Promise Frame.

Result:
Fixes #10748
@normanmaurer Out of curiosity, why do we have so many HTTP/2 implementations?
Can one of the admins verify this patch?

timeline.body: Why `2`?

reply.body: Just wanted to give Server and Client dedicated threads.

timeline.body: It looks like we return the newly created stream id in two places: as the return value and as the newly populated `http2FrameStream.id` field. What do you think about making the return value of this method `void` and using the latter when it's necessary? To me, that avoids the ambiguity up higher as to whether we should use `streamId` returned by this method or `pushPromiseFrame.pushStream().id()` (or the parallel in the `writeHeaders` method).
ffti: it's easier to read these branches if you put the simple case first and you get an added bonus of being able to drop the boolean not operator from the predicate.
Would it be easier to just add the tests to `Http2FrameCodecTest.java`? It already has a well developed testing scaffold.

reply.body: I tried but `Http2FrameCodecTest.java` was already big and complex and adding this made it 2x complex. So decided to move it into a separate test class.

timeline.body: In general, it's not a great idea to hard code ports for tests since you can't be sure they're available to you in all environments.
The meat of this looks good to me. I think the testing is a perhaps a bit more complex than it need be but perhaps I've missed something from the larger picture.
